subject.title: fix(qqbot): allow approval buttons in direct C2C conversations

question: For QQBot fallback approvals in direct C2C chats, which identity must authorize the callback when execApprovals is absent?
rationale: The patch assumes possession of any direct conversation is approval authority, while the existing security gate treats approval as explicit authority; source inspection cannot safely choose that trust policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Require trusted actor binding
options.body: Keep direct callbacks gated by an explicit, command-authorized, or request-bound trusted identity and repair the legitimate-owner path without authorizing every DM sender.

options.title: Treat C2C possession as authority
options.body: Intentionally allow any direct-chat sender to approve fallback requests, with explicit security documentation and live proof showing the accepted threat model.

recommendation.title: Require trusted actor binding
recommendation.body: Keep direct callbacks gated by an explicit, command-authorized, or request-bound trusted identity and repair the legitimate-owner path without authorizing every DM sender.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and proved the current fallback actor gate, so they have the clearest history context for the intended authorization invariant.
